Title: Google Launchpad Online now in Africa
Investment: We introduced the Start-up Launch program to hundreds of entrepreneurs in Uganda, Kenya, Nigeria, Senegal, and South Africa during the Google for Entrepreneurs week that ran from October 20th to 25th, and so far over 200 start-ups in Africa, and more than 3,000 entrepreneurs in 150 countries are taking advantage of the offering. We spoke to several entrepreneurs from Nairobi, Lagos, and South Africa about their experiences getting started in Africa - hear what they learned in these Spotlight videos.

Title: Elections in Nigeria - Technology as a tool for Democracy
Investment: As the country prepares for the governorship polls holding on April 11, voters continue to search for information on candidates, parties and polling units. To help voters find the information they’re looking for, in January we launched the Nigeria Elections Hub, and we continue to update it with news, Google+ Hangouts, and videos.

Title: Sawubona! Google for Nonprofits launches in South Africa, Kenya and Botswana.
Investment: Google launched its "Google for Nonprofits" program in South Africa, Kenya, and Botswana, providing eligible organizations with free access to tools and Google Ad Grants of up to $10,000 per month in advertising. The engagement also included the Google Academy for NGOs, a series of workshops focused on training South African nonprofits to effectively use digital tools.

Title: Bringing fast, affordable broadband to Ghana with Project Link
Investment: Through Project Link, Google is investing in metro fiber infrastructure to provide fast, affordable broadband in multiple cities in Ghana, beginning with Accra (Google Africa Blog). The project has already deployed over 700 kilometers of fiber in Kampala, Uganda, to support local internet service providers and academic institutions (Google Africa Blog).

Title: Investing in Africaâ€™s largest wind project
Investment: According to the Google Africa Blog, Google committed to investing in the Lake Turkana Wind Power Project in Northern Kenya by purchasing a 12.5% stake in the project from Vestas. This initiative, Africa's largest wind project, is designed to provide 310 megawatts of clean energy to Kenya's national grid, enough to power more than two million households.

Title: Bringing Better Wi-Fi to Kampala with Project Link
Investment: Google launched a Wi-Fi hotzone network across 120 sites in Kampala, Uganda, as part of its Project Link infrastructure initiative. This investment builds on a previously established fiber network to enable local mobile operators and ISPs to provide high-quality, affordable broadband access to the city's residents (Google Africa Blog).

Title: Investing in our teachers today for the students of tomorrow
Investment: Google invited colleges, universities, and educational nonprofits across Africa to apply for the 2016 Computer Science for High School (CS4HS) awards, which provide grants of up to $15,000 to fund teacher professional development in computer science (Google Africa Blog).

Title: Web Rangers in Africa: Promoting Online Safety
Investment: Google launched and expanded its Web Rangers online safety program in Africa, committing to train over 10,000 school pupils in Nigeria and expanding the initiative to 160 more schools in Kenya (Google Africa Blog). The program, which also launched in South Africa, provides digital citizenship and safety training to youth through face-to-face sessions and an online portal (Google Africa Blog).

Title: A growth engine for Africa: Training 1 million young people in digital skills
Investment: Google pledged to train 1 million young people across Africa in digital skills within one year by supporting programs like Digify Bytes and Digify Pro in partnership with Livity Africa. These free programs aim to help participants develop digital careers and become specialists for jobs in companies or digital agencies (Google Africa Blog).

Title: #DigitalskillsforAfrica: Over 500,000 people in Africa trained
Investment: Google committed to training 1 million Africans in digital skills within one year, reaching a milestone of over 500,000 people trained across the continent. The program includes face-to-face training and an online portal with 89 lessons to help individuals in countries like Kenya, Nigeria, and South Africa build businesses and create jobs.

Title: One million trained! But the task of getting Africa digital is just beginning.
Investment: Google successfully met its pledge to train 1 million young Africans in digital skills and announced an extension of the program to reach more communities outside urban centers. The initiative provides offline training in local languages (Swahili, IsiZulu, and Hausa) to students, job seekers, and business owners across Africa, with a commitment to ensuring at least 40% of trainees are women.

Title: Helping the leaders of tomorrow, read today.
Investment: Google.org awarded a $2 million grant to RTI International to enhance the Tangerine:Tutor platform, which supports Kenya's Tusome early literacy program. This investment, which also included technical support from Google volunteers, is part of Google.org's broader $50 million commitment to closing the global education gap through technology.

Title: CSquared Gets New Investors to Expand Internet Access in Africa
Investment: Google-led initiative CSquared is expanding its wholesale-only, carrier-neutral fiber optic networks across Africa through a partnership with Convergence Partners, IFC, and Mitsui. The project, which started as Google's Project Link, provides high-speed infrastructure in countries like Uganda and Ghana to support local entrepreneurs and businesses, while Google's Digital Skills for Africa program has trained over one million people on the continent.

Title: Google News Lab powers digital journalism training for 6,000 journalists in Africa
Investment: Google News Lab partnered with Code For Africa to launch a digital journalism training initiative to train more than 6,000 journalists across 12 major African cities by February 2018. The program provides training in skills such as mobile reporting, mapping, and data journalism through in-person sessions, a massive open online course (MOOC), and study groups Google Africa Blog.

Title: Making the internet work better for everyone in Africa
Investment: Google.org committed $20 million over five years to support nonprofits across Africa, including $5 million in grants through the 2018 Google.org Impact Challenge. The funding aims to improve lives and provides initial support for 400,000 low-income students in South Africa and Nigeria through partnerships with Gidi Mobile and Siyavula.

Title: Making computer science accessible to more students in Africa
Investment: Google provided funding to 60 community organizations across Africa to deliver computer science workshops to more than 50,000 students during Africa Code Week 2017. This initiative, executed in partnership with the Cape Town Science Centre, is part of Google's commitment to prepare 10 million people in Africa for future jobs.

Title: Launchpad comes to Africa to support tech startups! Apply to join the first accelerator class
Investment: Google launched the Launchpad Accelerator Africa program, which provides over $3 million in equity-free support, working space, and travel backing for tech startups in Ghana, Kenya, Nigeria, South Africa, Tanzania, and Uganda (Google Blog).

Title: Celebrating ten years of grants for CS educators
Investment: Google has funded nearly $13 million in global grants through its Computer Science (CS) educator professional development program (formerly CS4HS), with 61 universities and nonprofits in Africa receiving funding to support 5,000 educators across more than 15 countries.

Title: Launchpad Accelerator Africa: growing a community of startup influencers in Africa
Investment: Google committed over $3 million in equity-free support to more than 60 African tech startups over three years through the Launchpad Accelerator Africa program. The initiative provides mentorship, working space, and access to technology for startups across the continent, with the first cohort featuring 12 startups from Nigeria, Kenya, Ghana, South Africa, Tanzania, and Uganda.

Title: Announcing the 2018 Google Africa Scholarships!
Investment: Google announced the 2018 Google Africa Scholarships, providing 15,000 single-course and 500 nanodegree scholarships to aspiring and professional developers across Africa in partnership with Udacity and Andela (Google Blog). The program offered 10,000 scholarships to beginners and 5,000 to intermediate developers as part of a broader pledge to train ten million people on the continent (Google Blog).

Title: Announcing the Google Africa PhD Fellowship Program
Investment: Google announced the first four recipients of the Google Africa PhD Fellowship program, which provides funding to early-stage PhD students at African universities in computer science and related research areas. The inaugural fellows represent institutions in Morocco, Tanzania, Egypt, and South Africa (Google Africa Blog).

Title: Applications open for students leads in the Africa Developer Student Club program
Investment: Google launched the Developer Student Club (DSC) program in Africa as part of a broader commitment to provide mobile developer training to 100,000 developers across the continent. The program targets students in accredited colleges and universities, selecting Student Leads to facilitate workshops on technologies like Machine Learning and AI. Google Blog

Title: Google Impact Challenge, Africa: Empowering Africans to drive community impact
Investment: Google launched its first Google Impact Challenge in Africa, committing $6 million in funding to support nonprofits and social enterprises in Kenya, Nigeria, and South Africa. Each country was allocated $2 million to be awarded to winners and finalists as part of a larger $20 million five-year investment by Google.org in African nonprofits.

Title: Google AI in Ghana
Investment: Google announced the opening of a new AI research center in Accra, Ghana, to support machine learning research and collaborate with local universities. The post also highlights Google's ongoing commitment to provide digital skills training to 10 million Africans and support 100,000 developers through its Launchpad Accelerator Africa program (Google Africa Blog).

Title: Google for Nigeria: Making the internet more useful for more people
Investment: Google announced several major investments in Africa, including a $20 million Google.org commitment over five years, over $3 million in equity-free support for startups through Launchpad Accelerator Africa, and the rollout of Google Station Wi-Fi hotspots across 200 locations in five Nigerian cities.

Title: Announcing the finalists for the 2018 Google Impact Challenge Africa
Investment: Google is awarding $125,000 grants to each of the 36 finalists of the 2018 Google Impact Challenge Africa, totaling over $4.5 million in funding for nonprofits and social enterprises in Nigeria, Kenya, and South Africa. The finalists also receive training and support from Google to help scale their technology-driven solutions for community economic opportunity.

Title: Backing Africaâ€™s forward thinkers -- Meet the 2018 Google.org Impact Challenge winners
Investment: Google.org awarded grants to 36 nonprofit leaders and social entrepreneurs across Kenya, Nigeria, and South Africa as part of the 2018 Google Impact Challenge. Winners received $250,000 each and finalists received $125,000 to fund social innovation projects aimed at driving community impact (Google Africa Blog).

Title: Safer Internet Day 2019: Scaling our Online Safety Programmes in Africa
Investment: Google is scaling its "Be Internet Awesome" and "Web Rangers" online safety programs in Africa through major partnerships. In Nigeria, the initiative integrates safety content into the national curriculum to reach 56 million students annually, while in Kenya, a partnership with the Kenya Scouts Association aims to distribute safety guides to 1.4 million scouts.

Title: Celebrating International Women's Day 2019
Investment: Google is expanding its Womenwill initiative in Africa by adding 18 new chapters across Sub-Saharan Africa (bringing the total to 25) to provide women with digital skills, coaching, and mentorship. This commitment builds on Google's Digital Skills for Africa program, which has trained over 3 million people since 2016. Google Africa Blog

Title: Advance your career with the Google Africa Certifications Scholarships
Investment: Google announced 30,000 additional scholarship opportunities and 1,000 certification grants for Android, Web, and Cloud technologies for developers in Africa, as part of a larger commitment to provide mobile developer training to 100,000 Africans according to the Google Africa Blog.

Title: Inviting News Organizations in Africa, Middle East & Turkey to the Google News Initiative (GNI) Innovation Challenge
Investment: Google launched the Google News Initiative (GNI) Innovation Challenge for news organizations and startups in Africa, the Middle East, and Turkey, offering selected projects up to $150,000 in funding to support innovation in journalism (Google Africa Blog).

Title: Google supports Africa Code Week empowering over 100,000 students through Computer Science
Investment: Through the Grow with Google Community Microgrant, Google is funding 55 local organizations across 18 African countries to facilitate coding workshops for Africa Code Week, an initiative that has empowered over 100,000 students. This engagement supports Google's 2017 commitment to help 10 million Africans acquire digital skills for future jobs.

Title: Google for Kenya:  Preserving our culture, and helping Kenyan businesses to grow
Investment: Google's digital skills program has trained more than 4 million Africans, with an ultimate goal of reaching 10 million across the continent (Google Blog). Additionally, the company's Launchpad Accelerator Africa program has trained 60 startups, including Kenyan businesses such as Pezesha and Flexpay (Google Blog).

Title: Helping families in Africa stay safe online
Investment: Google provided grants to local organizations in Kenya, Nigeria, and South Africa to deliver online safety roadshows and partnered with government agencies to integrate safety curricula into national and regional school systems, including a program reaching 55,000 students in Kenya.

Title: Google Startup Week Lagos - helping Launchpad Accelerator Africa startups take their businesses global
Investment: Through the Launchpad Accelerator Africa program, Google provided 12 startups from its fourth cohort and 10 alumni startups with mentorship, working space, and travel support. Since its 2017 launch, the program has supported 47 startups that have collectively raised millions of dollars in investment and created hundreds of jobs across Africa (Google Blog).

Title: Announcing our first developer Space in Africa
Investment: Google launched its first Google Developers Space in Lagos, Nigeria, a physical hub designed to support African developers, entrepreneurs, and startups (Google Blog). The space houses the Google Launchpad Accelerator Africa and provides the tech community with free access to resources, workspace, and training (Google Blog).

Title: Funding 21 news projects in the Middle East, Africa and Turkey
Investment: Through the first Google News Initiative (GNI) Innovation Challenge for the Middle East, Turkey, and Africa, Google funded 21 news projects as part of its $300 million global commitment to journalism (Google Blog). The funding supported initiatives such as a "relevancy engine" for South Africa's Daily Maverick and personalization tools for Ringier Africa Digital Publishing in Nigeria (Google Blog).

Title: A Global Journalism Emergency Relief Fund for local news
Investment: Google launched the Journalism Emergency Relief Fund to provide grants ranging from a few thousand to tens of thousands of dollars to local news publishers globally, including in Africa, to support them during the COVID-19 pandemic. Additionally, Google.org committed $1 million to the International Center for Journalists and the Columbia Journalism School’s Dart Center to support reporters Google Africa Blog.

Title: Grow your skills with the Google Africa Developer Scholarships
Investment: Google announced 30,000 training scholarships and 1,000 grants for Associate Android Developer and Associate Cloud Engineer certifications for African developers, building on a commitment to provide 100,000 developers with training (Google Africa Blog).

Title: How we're responding to COVID-19 across Africa
Investment: Google committed $18.75 million in ad grants and credits for government agencies and small businesses in Africa, and Google.org provided a $4 million grant to the J-PAL Jobs and Opportunity Initiative focused on Sub-Saharan Africa as part of its COVID-19 response (Google Africa Blog).

Title: Improving mobile internet access through digital literacy
Investment: Google partnered with GSMA to introduce a new Android training module within the Mobile Internet Skills Training Toolkit (MISTT), aiming to empower 2 million people in Sub-Saharan Africa with mobile internet skills by 2021 (Google Africa Blog). This initiative focuses on improving digital literacy to help users understand and utilize the Android platform effectively (Google Africa Blog).

Title: Helping Africa restart the economy
Investment: Google committed over $5 million in grants and scholarships through Google.org, including $1 million for women in Kenya via GiveDirectly, $750k for IT scholarships, and $500k for small business training via the Praekelt Foundation across Kenya, South Africa, and Nigeria.

Title: Celebrating teachers leading in crisis and lifting others up on World Teacherâ€™s Day
Investment: Google committed to supporting 500,000 students and 25,000 teachers across Africa by providing access to G Suite for Education and the "Teach from Anywhere" initiative to facilitate distance learning (Google Africa Blog).

Title: YouTubeBlack Africa Creator Week- Supporting and Celebrating African Creators
Investment: Google is supporting African creators through the Africa Creator Week, which is part of a broader $100 million global fund dedicated to amplifying Black voices and perspectives on YouTube (Google Africa Blog). This initiative includes expert-led masterclasses and sessions focused on content strategy and monetization for creators across the continent (Google Africa Blog).

Title: Meet the African #YouTubeBlackVoices Creator Class of 2021
Investment: Google announced the inaugural African class of the #YouTubeBlack Voices Fund, providing seed funding and dedicated partner support to 23 creators and artists from Nigeria, South Africa, and Kenya. This initiative is part of a global, multi-year commitment to invest directly in Black creators to help them build their businesses and grow their reach on YouTube.

Title: Supporting Kenya's Economic Recovery
Investment: Google committed $10 million (approximately 1.1 billion Kenyan shillings) to support Kenya's economic recovery, including $2 million in Google.org grants for nonprofits, $3 million in small business loans, and $5 million for tech startups in Kenya.

Title: Internet Day: Safer with Google
Investment: Google.org awarded $1,000,000 through the Africa Online Safety Fund to 26 organizations across nine Sub-Saharan African countries to support innovative online safety initiatives. Grants ranged from $10,000 to $100,000 for non-profits and social enterprises in countries including Kenya, Nigeria, South Africa, and Ethiopia (Google Blog).

Title: Fostering innovation in Africa, the Middle East and Turkey
Investment: Google launched the second Google News Initiative Innovation Challenge for Africa, the Middle East, and Turkey, offering selected news organizations up to $150,000 each to fund projects that enhance reader engagement (Google Blog). The investment covers up to 70% of the total project costs for established publishers, startups, and industry associations in the region (Google Blog).

Title: A call for a better future for women and girls in Africa
Investment: Google launched the $25 million global Google.org Impact Challenge for Women and Girls to provide funding, mentoring, and support to nonprofits and social organizations worldwide, including in Africa, that are working to advance economic empowerment and prosperity for women and girls.

Title: Announcing new Google Career Certificates to help Africans learn new skills for digital jobs
Investment: Google announced three new Google Career Certificates in Africa, supported by a $750,000 Google.org grant to Junior Achievement Africa and the International Youth Foundation to provide 2,500 scholarships for vulnerable learners in Kenya, Nigeria, and South Africa.

Title: How fact checkers and Google.org are fighting misinformation.
Investment: Google.org provided a $2 million grant and a six-month pro-bono Google.org Fellowship to Full Fact to build AI tools for fact-checkers. This investment supports the work of Africa Check in South Africa, Nigeria, and Kenya to combat misinformation.

Title: Our continued commitment to helping grow the startup ecosystem in Africa
Investment: Google announced 40,000 developer scholarships for Android, Web, and Google Cloud development for African developers in partnership with Pluralsight and Andela. The blog post also opened applications for the Class 6 Google for Startups Accelerator Africa, providing three months of mentorship and product support to startups across 17 African countries.

Title: The Future is Africa: African Developers are Building for the World
Investment: Google is investing in Africa's developer ecosystem through the Google Africa Developer Scholarship program, which has provided 77,000 training opportunities and opened applications for an additional 40,000 spots in 2021. The engagement also includes the Google for Startups Accelerator Africa, which supports growth-stage startups with mentorship and resources across the continent.

Title: YouTube Announces Class of 2022 Application Date for the #YouTubeBlack Voices Fund
Investment: YouTube announced the opening of grant applications for the #YouTubeBlack Voices Fund Class of 2022, providing financial grants and dedicated support to Black creators and artists. The program expanded its eligibility to include creators from Sub-Saharan Africa, offering funding for production equipment, hiring teams, and professional development to help creators grow their channels.

Title: Supporting startups and SMEs in Africa
Investment: Google committed $6 million USD to support African entrepreneurship, consisting of a $3 million Black Founders Fund for startups and a $3 million Google.org grant to the Tony Elumelu Foundation. The funding provides non-dilutive capital, mentorship, and technical assistance to Black-led startups and women entrepreneurs across Africa.

Title: How weâ€™re supporting 14 new AI for Social Good projects in Sub Saharan Africa
Investment: Google announced funding, technical contributions, and computational resources for 14 new AI for Social Good projects across 10 Sub-Saharan African countries, including Uganda, Nigeria, Kenya, South Africa, and Ghana. The initiative, supported by Google.org and Google’s University Relations, provides grants to academics and nonprofits focusing on AI research for agriculture, conservation, and public health. Google Africa Blog

Title: YouTube Shorts arrives in Sub Saharan Africa
Investment: Google announced the launch of YouTube Shorts in Sub-Saharan Africa, noting that creators in the region would be eligible for the $100 million YouTube Shorts Fund to be distributed through 2022 Google Blog.

Title: Meet the 22 news innovators selected from the 2021 GNI Middle East, Turkey and Africa challenge
Investment: Through the 2021 Google News Initiative (GNI) Innovation Challenge, Google committed $2.1 million in funding to 22 news innovation projects across 14 countries in the Middle East, Turkey, and Africa. The funding supports various initiatives, such as AI-driven reader revenue bots in Kenya and hyperlocal journalism platforms in Zimbabwe, aimed at empowering local voices and developing sustainable news models.

Title: YouTube NextUp: Are you the next big thing on YouTube?
Investment: Google expanded its YouTube NextUp program to Sub-Saharan Africa, providing selected creators with a $1,000 voucher for production equipment and access to a week-long virtual Creator Camp. The initiative includes 1:1 mentoring and technical support to help fast-rising creators in the region grow their channels (Google Africa Blog).

Title: Meet The #YouTubeBlack Voices Music Class of 2022
Investment: Google is providing seed funding, dedicated partner support, and training programs to the #YouTubeBlack Voices Music Class of 2022, which includes artists and producers from Nigeria, South Africa, and Uganda (Google Africa Blog). Part of the #YouTubeBlack Voices Fund, this initiative invests directly in the development of participants' channels to amplify Black voices, though specific funding amounts are not disclosed in the post (Google Africa Blog).

Title: Supporting Journalism in Africa
Investment: Google is increasing its investment in African journalism through the Google News Initiative (GNI), which includes a partnership with UNESCO for journalist training, a News Lab Team, and Innovation Challenges that fund publishers' digital transformation. The initiative also supported the Sinelizwi citizen journalism project, which trained 62 citizens from all nine provinces in South Africa (Google Africa Blog).

Title: Applications open for the Google for Startups Accelerator Africa Class 7
Investment: Google announced the opening of applications for the seventh cohort of the Google for Startups Accelerator Africa, a program providing three months of mentorship and technical support to tech startups across the continent. Since its launch in 2017, the initiative has supported 82 startups from 17 African countries, whose alumni have collectively raised over $117 million in funding and created more than 2,800 jobs (Google Blog).

Title: Supporting Journalism in South Africa
Investment: Through the Google News Initiative Innovation Challenge, Google provided $260,000 (ZAR 4,459,000) to three South African news projects—Food for Mzansi, Daily Maverick, and Scrolla.Africa—to support digital innovation in journalism (Google Africa Blog). Additionally, Google partnered with UNESCO to support over 100 journalism schools across Africa and provided training to over 17,000 journalists through the Google News Lab (Google Africa Blog).

Title: Seeking news innovators in Middle East, Turkey & Africa
Investment: Google launched a new round of the Google News Initiative (GNI) Innovation Challenge for the Middle East, Turkey, and Africa, offering funding of up to $150,000 per project to support digital news innovation. The program is open to news organizations, startups, and freelancers in the region to develop projects that increase reader engagement or explore new business models. Google Blog

Title: Helping Africans create their own opportunities
Investment: Google.org committed $3 million to the Tony Elumelu Foundation (TEF) to support 500 female entrepreneurs across Africa. The initiative also includes the first Google.org Fellowship in Sub-Saharan Africa, providing technical and business expertise to help TEF scale its digital platform for entrepreneurs.

Title: The Equiano subsea cable has arrived in Togo, first stop in Africa
Investment: Google's Equiano subsea cable has arrived in Lomé, Togo, as the first stop in an infrastructure project connecting Europe with Togo, Nigeria, Namibia, South Africa, and St. Helena (Google Africa Blog). The cable is expected to provide approximately 20 times more network capacity than the last cable built to serve the region, aiming to improve internet speed and affordability (Google Africa Blog).

Title: Google at the African Union
Investment: Google committed to investing $1 billion over five years to support Africa’s digital transformation and has provided over $16 million in grants to more than 50 African nonprofits (Google Blog). This engagement includes training 6 million young Africans in digital skills and partnering with the African Union to enable internet access and facilitate digital trade (Google Blog).

Title: Weâ€™re hiring for our first product development center in Africa
Investment: Google announced the opening of its first product development center in Nairobi, Kenya, as part of its broader $1 billion investment commitment to support Africa's digital transformation over five years (Google Blog). The center is hiring for engineering and product roles to create transformative products and services for people in Africa and globally (Google Blog).

Title: Equianoâ€™s next stop is in Nigeria
Investment: Google has invested in the Equiano subsea cable infrastructure, which recently completed its landing in Lagos, Nigeria, to provide faster, more affordable internet. The project, which also includes landings in Togo and South Africa, aims to support Nigeria's digital transformation through partnerships with local telecom players like the West Indian Ocean Cable Company (WIOCC).

Title: Announcing Google Africa Developer Scholarship, Class 5
Investment: Google announced 30,000 additional Android and Google Cloud training scholarships for aspiring and professional developers across Africa as part of the fifth year of the Google Africa Developer Scholarship program, in partnership with Andela and Pluralsight.

Title: A Digital Growth Program for Publishers in South Africa
Investment: Google, through the Google News Initiative and in partnership with FT Strategies, hosted the Digital Immersion Program in South Africa to provide training and skills to journalists and publishers. The program helped local, community, and national news organizations develop sustainable online business models and navigate digital transformation.

Title: Announcing the Black Founders Fund 2022
Investment: Google announced a second $4 million Black Founders Fund in Africa to provide 60 startups with up to $100,000 each in equity-free cash awards, paired with Google Cloud credits and technical support (Google Africa Blog).

Title: Google Research enhances its AI growth in Africa
Investment: Google inaugurated a new AI research center in Ghana and announced a product development center in Nairobi as part of its $1 billion five-year investment plan for Africa. The initiatives include funding for the African Master’s in Machine Intelligence program, scholarships for female computer science students, and research agreements with universities in Ghana and Kenya.

Title: Innovation success in Middle East, Africa and Turkey
Investment: Google announced 34 recipients of the 3rd Google News Initiative (GNI) Innovation Challenge for the Middle East, Turkey, and Africa, which funds projects such as automated fact-checking and disability-inclusive news apps in countries like Nigeria, Kenya, South Africa, and Uganda. The program is part of Google's broader $300 million global commitment to help journalism thrive in the digital age (Google Blog).

Title: Supporting Small Businesses and Youth-led Startups in Africa
Investment: Google established a partnership with the African Union Commission (AUC) to support youth-led startups and small businesses across Africa through digital skills training, the Hustle Academy, and the Google for Startups Accelerator. This collaboration leverages Google's existing commitment to train 10 million young Africans and SMBs in digital skills (Google Africa Blog).

Title: Supporting Natural Language Processing (NLP)  in Africa
Investment: Google is advancing language technologies in Africa through its AI research center in Ghana, support for the Lacuna Fund to close data gaps, and partnerships with Zindi and Data Scientists Network for NLP hackathons and workshops across countries like Nigeria, Kenya, and Tanzania (Google Africa Blog).

Title: Meet Google for Startups Black Founders Fund in Africa 2022 Startups
Investment: Google announced 60 startups from 10 African countries as recipients of the 2022 Google for Startups Black Founders Fund. Each startup receives $100,000 in non-dilutive cash awards and up to $200,000 in Google Cloud credits, along with mentorship and technical support. Google Africa Blog

Title: Delivering on our $1B commitment in Africa
Investment: Google is delivering on its $1 billion commitment to Africa (Google Blog) by establishing its first African cloud region in South Africa and a product development center in Nairobi. The investment includes over $22 million in Google.org funding for nonprofits and skills training, such as a $3 million grant for air quality monitoring and $1.5 million for career certifications (Google Blog).

Title: Supporting African news organisations who are advancing media literacy
Investment: Google is supporting African news organizations through the Google News Initiative (GNI), which includes funding for Dubawa to train 500 journalists across Nigeria, Ghana, Sierra Leone, Liberia, and The Gambia. The engagement also features a news delivery pilot using RCS in collaboration with Fathm and publishers in South Africa, Nigeria, and Kenya, alongside support for the Africa Facts summit.

Title: Helping African job seekers prepare for interviews
Investment: Google is supporting the African workforce through its commitment to train 10 million Africans in digital skills, with over 6 million people already trained through Grow with Google programs like Google Career Certificates and Google Africa Developer Scholarships. This engagement includes providing AI-powered tools like "Interview Warmup" to help job seekers in Africa prepare for roles in high-growth fields such as data analytics and IT support.

Title: Meet The YouTube Black Voices Creator, Artist, Singer and Songwriter Class of 2023
Investment: Through the YouTube Black Voices Fund, Google is providing grants, seed funding, and dedicated partner support to its Class of 2023, which includes 179 creators globally. The program specifically highlights a cohort of creators from Sub-Saharan Africa as part of this multi-year commitment to amplify Black voices and content on the platform (Google Africa Blog).

Title: A mission to ensure a safe digital experience in Africa
Investment: Google.org provided a $1 million grant to the Impact Amplifier Foundation to launch the second cohort of the Africa Online Safety Fund, which supports organizations dedicated to enhancing online safety in Africa (Google Africa Blog).

Title: Nigerian fact checkers fight election misinformation with Full Fact's AI Tools
Investment: Through Google.org, Google provided a multi-year grant and pro bono technical support from seven Fellows to Full Fact to develop AI tools used by 23 Nigerian fact-checkers to combat election misinformation (Google Africa Blog). The engagement includes a commitment to support the organization for another three years to scale these tools globally and provide ongoing training to local partners like Africa Check and Dubawa (Google Africa Blog).

Title: Apply for the Google for Startups Black Founders Fund 2023
Investment: Google announced the opening of applications for the 2023 Black Founders Fund in Africa, a program that provides capital and resources to early-stage and growth-phase technology startups led by Black founders. The initiative aims to support entrepreneurs across the African continent in scaling their businesses and overcoming systemic funding barriers, building on a 2022 cohort that supported 110 startups.

Title: Championing Women in Africa on International Womenâ€™s Day
Investment: Google announced the inaugural cohort of 15 women-led startups for the Google for Startups Accelerator: Women Founders (Africa) and launched the Hustle Academy bootcamp to provide training and mentorship for women-led SMEs across Africa Google Blog.

Title: Empowering the next generation of tech innovators in Sub-Saharan Africa
Investment: Google is expanding its CS First program in Kenya, Nigeria, and South Africa through a partnership with the Cape Town Science Center, aiming to train over 10,000 students in digital and coding skills. The initiative involves supporting a network of local non-profit organizations and educational institutions to run computer science workshops for elementary and middle school students.

Title: Announcing the new Google career certificate in cybersecurity with 2000 scholarships for Africans
Investment: Google is providing 2,000 scholarships for its new Cybersecurity Career Certificate to learners across Sub-Saharan Africa (Google Africa Blog). The program, delivered on Coursera, aims to address the cybersecurity skills gap through partnerships with local organizations including the ICT Authority in Kenya, The Roothub in Nigeria, and RLabs in South Africa.

Title: Announcing the inaugural Google for Startups Accelerator: Climate Change program in the Middle East and Africa!
Investment: Google announced the inaugural Google for Startups Accelerator: Climate Change, a 10-week equity-free program for Seed to Series A startups in the Middle East and Africa. Selected startups receive mentorship, workshops on product design and business growth, and Google Cloud credits via the Google for Startups Cloud Program (Google Africa Blog).

Title: Announcing the 2023 Black Founders Fund Cohort in Africa
Investment: Google selected 25 African startups for its 2023 Black Founders Fund, providing each with up to $150,000 in non-dilutive cash and $200,000 in Google Cloud credits. This engagement aims to address VC funding inequality by supporting Black-led startups across countries including Nigeria, Kenya, and South Africa with capital, mentoring, and technical resources.

Title: Unlocking Africa's Potential - Why Digital Skills are Crucial for the Future of Work
Investment: Google is collaborating with the African Union Commission to provide Hustle Academy training as part of a Digital Skills Campaign aiming to reach 100,000 young people across Africa by 2024. The program offers free five-day bootcamps for entrepreneurs and has already reached approximately 1,000 participants in Ethiopia, Madagascar, Ghana, and South Sudan (Google Africa Blog).

Title: Google for Startups Accelerator: AI First Program. Call for Applications
Investment: Google announced a call for applications for its "Google for Startups Accelerator: AI First" program, a 10-week equity-free accelerator for African startups (seed to Series A) or those building Africa-centered AI solutions. The program provides mentorship, AI expertise, and access to Google Cloud Platform resources, building on Google's initiative that has supported 106 startups across 17 African nations since 2018.

Title: Supporting digital transformation through South Africa's SMEs
Investment: Google has supported over 4,000 South African SME graduates through its Hustle Academy, a five-day virtual bootcamp providing upskilling, mentorship, and networking opportunities. The program focuses on accelerating digital transformation and economic growth for small businesses in South Africa.

Title: Introducing Our New Cohort for the Google for Startups Accelerator: AI First Program

Title: 5 ways Google is accelerating Health AI innovation in Africa

Title: The Journey of African SMBs: Reflecting on Google's Hustle Academy Impact

Title: A look ahead at the AU Summit and Africa Business Forum
Investment: Google is co-hosting the Africa Business Forum 2024 and supporting digital transformation through initiatives like the Digital Futures Project for AI research and the Google Career Certificates program, which has reached over 20,000 graduates in Africa (Google Africa Blog). Title: How Google is Supporting Election Integrity in South Africa
Investment: Google is funding a fact-checking coalition led by Africa Check in South Africa and supporting six additional fact-checking coalitions across the continent through the Google News Initiative. Title: Inviting applications for the Google Startups Accelerator Africa
Investment: Google is inviting applications for the 2024 cohort of the Google for Startups Accelerator Africa, providing Seed to Series A tech startups in Africa with equity-free support including up to $350,000 in Google Cloud credits, mentorship, and technical workshops (Google Blog).

Title: Inviting applications for the 2024 Hustle Academy
Investment: Google is inviting applications for the 2024 cohort of its Hustle Academy, a training program for SMBs in Kenya, Nigeria, and South Africa that has supported over 10,000 participants since 2022. The program provides training in business skills and AI, and has previously provided grants to participants to help them access additional funding sources.

Title: Support for those affected by Kenya's flood crisis
Investment: Google.org committed $250,000 in emergency relief grants to support communities in Kenya affected by the devastating flood crisis that displaced 200,000 people.

Title: Improving connectivity and accelerating economic growth across Africa with new investments
Investment: Google announced Umoja, the first fiber optic cable to connect Africa (anchored in Kenya) to Australia, passing through several countries including Uganda, Rwanda, and South Africa. This initiative is part of Google's previously announced $1 billion commitment to Africa's digital transformation, which also includes a new cybersecurity collaboration with the Kenyan government.

Title: Meet the 24 startups advancing healthcare with AI
Investment: Google selected 24 startups, including six from Nigeria, Egypt, Kenya, and South Africa, for its Growth Academy: AI for Health program. The initiative provides three months of mentorship and product support to help these companies scale AI-driven healthcare solutions across Africa and other regions; no specific funding amount was mentioned.

Title: African Startups: Driving Innovation and Economic Growth

The program also offers participants mentorship and access to Google’s AI tools and infrastructure to scale their solutions (Google Africa Blog).

Investment: Google is executing a $1 billion investment commitment in Sub-Saharan Africa, which includes infrastructure projects like the Equiano subsea cable and initiatives to support local entrepreneurs and digital skills. This funding, originally announced in 2021, aims to drive economic growth and innovation across the continent, contributing to an estimated $16 billion in economic activity in 2023 according to a report by Public First.

Title: Africa's AI Moment: Building a future powered by technology and talent
Investment: Google announced a $5.8 million commitment to accelerate AI skilling initiatives across Sub-Saharan Africa, targeting workers, teenagers, non-profit leaders, and the public sector (Google Blog). The investment includes support for Nigeria's Federal Ministry of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy and an equity-free accelerator fund for Nigerian AI startups (Google Blog).

Title: Supporting Startups in Africa: The Power of Empowering Black Entrepreneurs
Investment: Through the Black Founders Fund, Google provides non-dilutive funding, mentorship, and resources to Black-led startups across Africa. Since 2021, the program has supported over 220 startups in Africa and Europe, helping them raise $379 million in follow-on funding and create more than 6,000 jobs (Google Blog).

Title: A Blueprint for a New Era of African Innovation
Investment: Google is investing $1 billion to support Africa's digital transformation, which includes infrastructure like the Equiano and Umoja subsea cables and research centers in Accra and Nairobi (Google Africa Blog). Additionally, the company recently committed $5.8 million to accelerate AI skilling initiatives across the continent to empower people in an AI-powered world (Google Africa Blog).

Title: A robotics program transforming AI education across Africa
Investment: Google, in collaboration with UNESCO and Infinix, launched the CogLabs robotics and AI education program as part of its $1 billion investment commitment to Africa. The initiative provides hands-on training using 3D-printed kits and smartphones, having already reached over 10,000 teachers and students across 35 countries.

Title: Advanced Flood Hub features for aid organizations and governments
Investment: Google.org provided funding to GiveDirectly and the International Rescue Committee to deliver AI-powered cash relief to 7,500 people in Nigeria. This investment, mentioned as a key collaboration in the Google Blog, enabled families in Kogi and Benue states to receive financial support 5-7 days before peak flooding.

Title: Google Cloud launches cybersecurity trainings in South Africa
Investment: As part of its $1 billion commitment in Africa, Google Cloud launched the Cybersecurity Upskilling Initiative in South Africa to provide training for job seekers and 1,000 public service employees. The initiative, in partnership with NEMISA and the Department for Public Service and Administration, aims to address the cybersecurity skills gap in the country.

Title: Google Hustle Academy 2025 Applications Open
Investment: Google is providing free virtual AI and business training to SMBs in Kenya, Nigeria, and South Africa through its Hustle Academy 2025 program. The initiative has reached a significant scale, having already skilled over 15,000 SMBs across Africa since its launch in 2022 (Google Africa Blog).

Title: A sustainable future for South African news requires innovation and collaboration between platforms and publishers
Investment: Google partnered with the Association of Independent Publishers to launch the R114 million Digital News Transformation Fund, aimed at helping independent, community, and local news publishers in South Africa build resilient digital businesses (Google Africa Blog).

Investment: Google is supporting online businesses in South Africa through a bootcamp-style digital marketing training program, an Ad Credits Program to boost digital presence, and interest-free microloans administered by Thundafund to fund strategic growth investments (Google Africa Blog).

Investment: Google has opened applications for the 2025 cohort of its Google for Startups Accelerator Africa program, which provides Seed to Series A tech startups across Africa with up to $350,000 in Google Cloud credits and equity-free support (Google Africa Blog). Investment: Google has selected 10 startups for the second cohort of the Google for Startups Accelerator: South Africa Program, providing them with equity-free funding, mentorship, and technical workshops to support growth in sectors like fintech, health, and energy. Investment: Google launched the Digital Growth Initiative for South African businesses, providing advanced digital marketing training via the Ads Academy, ad credits to enhance digital presence, and grant opportunities administered by Thundafund for strategic business investments. Investment: Google is implementing a five-year support plan for the South African news industry, which includes targeted investments through the Digital News Transformation Fund and Google News Showcase, investment in AI-driven innovation, and foundational training for journalists.
